instrument_framework: EU Artificial Intelligence Act — Article 5 manipulation prohibitions
scope: Binding prohibition only where the cumulative Article 5(1)(a) or (b) conditions are met; not a general ban on persuasion or political manipulation.
material_exclusions: Subtle cumulative influence may fail material-distortion, causation, or significant-harm thresholds.

instrument_framework: EU Artificial Intelligence Act — GPAI systemic-risk duties
scope: Binding evaluation/adversarial testing, systemic-risk assessment and mitigation, serious-incident reporting and cybersecurity for GPAI with systemic risk; methods are not fixed to the Code or NIST.
material_exclusions: No validated cumulative-agency metric or benchmark-to-release threshold; near misses are not automatically statutory serious incidents.

instrument_framework: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
scope: Voluntary means to demonstrate compliance with binding GPAI duties; alternative adequate means remain permitted.
material_exclusions: Code commitments are not standalone statutory rights or duties and do not create a manipulation score-to-release threshold.

instrument_framework: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency duties and Code of Practice
scope: Binding marking/disclosure duties; the supporting Code is voluntary. Article 50(2) pre-existing generators have a limited transition to 2026-12-02.
material_exclusions: Metadata can be stripped; provenance does not cover truthful personalized, conversational or relational influence.

instrument_framework: Digital Services Act Articles 25, 34–35, 37–40
scope: Article 25/27 platform duties plus VLOP/VLOSE-only Articles 34–35, 37–40. Electoral systemic-risk duties and non-profiled recommender choice are not platform-wide.
material_exclusions: VLOP/VLOSE scope leaves many assistants, smaller services, and off-platform activity outside.

instrument_framework: DSA election-risk guidelines and toolkit
scope: Election-specific risk assessment, recommender mitigation, generative AI, incident response, exercises, and post-election review.
material_exclusions: Guidelines are not a standalone law; causal effectiveness remains under-evaluated.

instrument_framework: Regulation on transparency and targeting of political advertising
scope: Defined political advertising only. Restricts personal-data targeting, prohibits special-category profiling and establishes a broader EU online repository architecture.
material_exclusions: Organic influence, issue advocacy, proxies, and private conversational steering can evade ad classification.

instrument_framework: General Data Protection Regulation
scope: Purpose limitation, minimization, transparency, profiling, rights, DPIAs, and portability for personal data.
material_exclusions: Portability and deletion of inferred, embedded, or relational assistant state are unsettled.

instrument_framework: Digital Markets Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/1925
scope: Contestability and fairness duties for Commission-designated gatekeepers and the core platform services listed in their designation decisions; virtual assistants are expressly a core platform service. Relevant duties include defaults and user choice, interoperability, data access and portability, and restrictions on self-preferencing and combining or using data.
material_exclusions: Core-platform-service status or being an AI assistant does not itself trigger duties: the undertaking and service must be designated. The DMA protects contestability and fairness, not manipulation or agency as such; limited suspension or exemption routes exist.
authority_owner: European Commission (sole enforcer; national authorities may support)

instrument_framework: EU Data Act
scope: Cloud switching and interoperability duties; progressive removal of switching charges.
material_exclusions: Model, memory, embedding, agent, and evaluation portability remain incomplete.

instrument_framework: European Media Freedom Act
scope: Media pluralism, independence, concentration assessment, and platform-media safeguards.
material_exclusions: Generative answer-layer source selection and omission are not fully covered.
authority_owner: European Commission; European Board for Media Services

instrument_framework: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
status: Not yet in force as of 2026-08-11
scope: Adopted treaty text; EU ratified 2026-05-15, but Article 30 entry threshold remains unmet.
material_exclusions: High-level duties require entry into force and domestic operationalization; private-sector coverage can vary by implementation choice.

instrument_framework: HUDERIA methodology
scope: Non-legally binding human-rights, democracy and rule-of-law assessment guidance.
material_exclusions: Agency-transfer construct and longitudinal measures are not yet standardized.

instrument_framework: Brazil TSE Resolutions 23.610 and 23.755/2026
scope: Synthetic-content rules, deepfake prohibition, anti-favoritism, recommender duties, plan/evidence obligations and a narrow corrective-promotion remedy; no general official-source-grounding duty.
material_exclusions: The 72h/24h rule and assistant neutrality are unusually broad; same-reach correction is not a general right and effect evidence remains open.

instrument_framework: FCC Telephone Consumer Protection Act declaratory ruling
scope: AI-generated voices in robocalls are treated as artificial or prerecorded voices requiring consent and applicable disclosures.
material_exclusions: Does not cover every channel, truthful persuasion, or foreign/offshore operations.

instrument_framework: NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile
scope: Generative-AI risk identification, measurement, management, monitoring, provenance, incident, and governance practices.
material_exclusions: Voluntary; no election-specific or binding release threshold.

instrument_framework: C2PA Technical Specification 2.4
scope: Cryptographically signed content credentials and provenance assertions.
material_exclusions: Participation gaps, stripping, laundering, capture-chain gaps, and no protection against truthful manipulation.
authority_owner: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity

instrument_framework: Canada Directive on Automated Decision-Making
scope: Impact assessment, testing, peer review, notice, explanation, human intervention, recourse, and contingency controls.
material_exclusions: Self-scoring, scope limits, and weak adaptation to general-purpose or generative systems.

instrument_framework: UK Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS)
legal_force: Mandatory administrative policy within scope; recommended elsewhere
scope: Publication of an ATRS record for Beta/Pilot or Production algorithmic tools used by in-scope central-government organisations where the tool significantly influences a decision with public effect or directly interacts with the public.
material_exclusions: The mandate does not generally extend beyond central government; broad-policy analytical models and pre-Beta tools are normally outside mandatory scope. FOIA, EIR and data-protection exemptions permit withholding or reducing sensitive information, exceptionally including the existence of a tool.
authority_owner: Government Digital Service; each in-scope central-government organisation
application_publication: Mandate announced 2024-02-06; mandatory scope and exemptions policy published 2024-12-17; guidance updated 2025-05-08

instrument_framework: Frontier AI Safety Commitments — AI Seoul Summit 2024
status: Voluntary commitments agreed by 20 listed organisations after the 2025-02-07 update; implementation is organisation-specific
scope: Frontier AI models and systems only: lifecycle severe-risk assessment, evaluative input, measurable risk thresholds, mitigations, stop-development or stop-deployment processes where risks cannot be kept below thresholds, internal accountability, and public or trusted-actor transparency.
material_exclusions: Voluntary and limited to signatories and frontier AI; signatories may evolve their approaches. Public disclosure can be limited for risk or disproportionate commercial sensitivity. The text creates no common enforcement mechanism and no comprehensive democratic-manipulation regime.
authority_owner: Signatory organisations; UK and Republic of Korea governments (announcers)

instrument_framework: EU AI Act — Annex III 8(b) election-influence systems
status: Listed high-risk use case; main duties apply 2027-12-02
scope: Systems intended to influence election/referendum outcomes or voting behaviour with direct exposure; administrative/logistical campaign tools excluded.
material_exclusions: Administrative or logistical campaign tools that do not directly influence voters are excluded; obligations are not yet generally applicable.

instrument_framework: Code of Conduct on Disinformation under the DSA
status: Auditable for signatories since 2025-07-01; first post-integration reports published 2026-03-24
scope: Demonetisation, political ads, coordinated manipulation, bots/impersonation/deepfakes, recommenders, researchers and election rapid response.
material_exclusions: Commitments bind signatories through the code route, not all services; causal effect and private-channel coverage remain limited.

instrument_framework: TSE Portaria 463/2026 — electoral compliance plans
status: In force; plans due 2026-08-16; consolidated implementation reports due 2026-12-19
scope: Operationalises platform plans for social, messaging, video, search and generative/conversational AI: concrete controls, metrics, timelines, impact assessment, evidence preservation, channels and reporting.
material_exclusions: Proportional-diligence regime rather than a guarantee of election outcomes; self-chosen indicators and limited independent access can weaken evaluation.

instrument_framework: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (Directive 2005/29/EC) and 2021 Commission guidance
legal_force: Binding directive via national transposition; non-binding Commission guidance
status: Directive in force and national measures applicable; 2021 Commission guidance operational
scope: Unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices before, during and after a transaction in relation to a product. The guidance expressly covers algorithms, AI, targeting, algorithmic personalisation, recommender systems, data-driven persuasion and dark patterns when the UCPD tests are met.
material_exclusions: Generally excludes non-commercial or electoral persuasion, B2B-only conduct and interests other than consumers' economic interests; requires a trader, consumer, product-related commercial practice and actual or likely effect on a transactional decision. More specific EU rules prevail in case of conflict. The guidance itself has no legal force.
authority_owner: Member-State courts and administrative consumer authorities; European Commission coordination and guidance
application_publication: Directive published 2005-06-11; national measures applicable by 2007-12-12; guidance published 2021-12-29; current applicable consolidation dated 2022-05-28

instrument_framework: UK Online Safety Act — one-to-one chatbot coverage boundary
scope: Covers regulated search and user-to-user services, illegal content duties and specified harmful-content regimes.
material_exclusions: A provider's one-to-one generative chatbot output is generally outside Part 3 unless another regulated function applies; lawful political misinformation is not a general regulated category.

instrument_framework: New York AI companion chatbot safeguards
status: Enacted 2025; state implementation applies under the enacted provisions
scope: Disclosure that the system is not human, periodic reminders during sustained use and a protocol for self-harm or suicide expressions.
material_exclusions: Relational-safety precedent, not evidence of political dependence or democratic agency transfer; jurisdiction and service definitions are narrow.

instrument_framework: EU Digital Fairness Act — planned Commission initiative
legal_force: Planned legislative initiative; no legal force
status: Under preparation; Commission legislative initiative scheduled for Q4 2026 on an indicative timetable; no proposal adopted as of 2026-08-13
scope: Officially stated intended scope includes dark patterns, addictive design of digital products, unfair personalisation, misleading influencer marketing, unfair price-marketing practices and digital-contract issues, with particular attention to vulnerable consumers and minors.
material_exclusions: No legislative text, duties, thresholds, addressees, enforcement model or final scope yet. Official materials do not specifically promise AI-assistant transparency. The initiative is consumer/commercial in orientation and must not be coded as an implemented intervention or evidence of effectiveness.
authority_owner: European Commission (preparation); European Parliament and Council only after a proposal
application_publication: 2026 work programme published 2025-10-21; planned Q4 2026 proposal (indicative)

instrument_framework: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative
scope: Agent standards and protocols, identity/authentication/authorization research, and security evaluation methods.
material_exclusions: Voluntary and security-led; does not itself establish root-purpose provenance, political safeguards or a binding deployment gate.
